extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: An elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models, comprising 1,500 human-curated samples selected to require visual dependency, minimize data leakage, and assess 6 core capabilities across 18 detailed axes.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.publisher: Shanghai AI Laboratory; University of Science and Technology of China; The Chinese University of Hong Kong
extraction.citeAs: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao. Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were roughly selected from existing multimodal benchmarks using an automated pipeline, then filtered by LLM inspectors for visual dependency and leakage, and finally manually reviewed and curated by experts to produce the final benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing benchmark samples drawn from MMMU, MMBench, ScienceQA, AI2D, SEED-Bench, and MathVista; the paper states two benchmarks focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: An automated coarse-filtering pipeline was applied using two closed-source and six open-source LLM inspectors; samples with more than two hits were excluded. Remaining samples were split into difficulty categories using LVLM hit counts, then manually curated into 1,500 final samples.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Samples were filtered to retain only those with hit counts of two or fewer among LLM inspectors, indicating around 75% of inspectors failed to answer correctly; manual review further ensured visual dependency, minimal leakage, and coverage of capability dimensions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review and selection to ensure each sample's answer depended on visual content, covered capability dimensions, and required advanced multimodal abilities. The benchmark is multiple-choice formatted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports hit counts from 16 LVLMs and uses them to split samples into difficulty categories (easy, moderate, hard, tough) before final manual curation; no inter-annotator disagreement analysis is described.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three experts; no further demographic details are provided.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Two closed-source LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro) and six open-source LLMs (including LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B) were used as automated inspectors; evaluation and experiments were conducted in a codebase modified from VLMEvalKit.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states a future plan to expand MMStar into a larger online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage; no formal versioning or deprecation policy is given.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve fairness and reliability in LVLM evaluation by reducing misjudgments caused by text-only solvable samples and training-data leakage, thereby avoiding misleading comparisons and misguidance in multimodal research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies two major sources of bias in existing benchmarks: samples that do not require visual content and unintentional data leakage from training corpora. MMStar is designed to mitigate these issues.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that existing benchmarks can contain samples solvable without images or leaked into training data, which can misjudge actual multimodal gains. For MMStar, no explicit limitations beyond future expansion are stated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of large vision-language models; benchmarking accuracy, multimodal gain, and multimodal leakage. The paper uses MMStar for testing and comparison of LVLMs, not for training.
